links.outcome: Valid SNOMED CT term match and exact match rates for RAG-grounded versus other GPT-4 mapping approaches
links.effect: RAG had 96.2% valid term match and 57.6% exact match, versus fine-tuned 69.2% valid and 47.2% exact; RAG structural errors were 14%, lower than other models.
links.quote: The RAG model achieved the highest performance with a 96.2% valid SNOMED CT term match rate and a 57.6% overall exact match rate, surpassing the fine-tuned model (69.2% valid term match, 47.2% exact match).

screen.practice: retrieval grounding (RAG) and prompt engineering for terminology mapping
screen.reason: Evaluated the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and prompt engineering to an existing LLM (GPT-4) compared to baseline for clinical terminology mapping.
